correctness.rationale: The primary full text gives \(J_L=\operatorname{diag}(1+h-hg,1+h-h\zeta)\). Under \(0<g<1\), \(0<\zeta<1\), and \(h>0\), both entries are strictly greater than one, so the fixed point is a hyperbolic source. The source's printed sink thresholds \(2/(g-1)\) and \(2/(\zeta-1)\) are both negative, so every positive \(h\) satisfies the printed sink condition. The exact witness \(g=1/2\), \(\zeta=1/3\), \(h=1\) gives multipliers \(3/2\) and \(5/3\) and thresholds \(-4\) and \(-3\). No finite experiment is used for the universal conclusion.
